text:
Alex S: tagging the night crew. handing off ongoing memory/eviction noise affecting embeddings in us-west-2.
Maya P: seen the alerts, thanks. can you summarize current state and mitigations so far? :eyes:
Alex S: summary — starting ~22:10 UTC we saw a sustained spike in kv-cache evictions on the embeddings tier (us-west-2). eviction-rate jumped from ~0.5/s -> 5-8/s. associated symptom: elevated embeddings latency (p50 up 2x) and a small but growing number of 429s for short embedding requests.
Alex S: incident bot created INC-2026-77 at 22:15 UTC — bridge is open. deploy-bot posted the scale action at 22:22.
SRE Bot: [incident INC-2026-77] bridge: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-77 | severity: P2 | owner: alex.s
Alex S: what we did so far:
- temporarily increased replica count for embeddings-cache-worker from 6 -> 9 (kubectl patch) — reduced instant eviction pressure but not fully back to baseline
- lowered cache eviction aggressiveness (kv.threshold -> 0.75) via feature flag in configstore
- disabled prefetching for new embeddings requests (hotfix flag) to cut background writes
- rate-limited high RPS customers on the routing layer as a precaution
Alex S: immediate impact: evictions down ~30%, latency improved p50 but p95 still elevated, crashes not observed. customers impacted: a handful of high-throughput embedding customers experiencing timeouts and some 429s. no broad outage.
Maya P: good. are runbook steps and commands in the bridge notes? send the quick commands block please.
Alex S: pasted below — basic commands we used:
```
# increase replicas
kubectl -n embeddings scale deploy/embeddings-cache-worker --replicas=9
# view eviction metrics
kubectl -n monitoring port-forward svc/prometheus 9090:9090 &
# patch feature flag
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://configstore.internal/api/flags/kv_eviction_threshold \
  -d '{"value":0.75}'
```
Alex S: runbook pointers: https://redwood.docs/runbooks/kv-eviction (see section 3.2 for tuning thresholds), and the embeddings playbook https://redwood.docs/runbooks/embeddings-anomalies
Maya P: noted. I'm taking primary for the next 4h. Raj, you'll be secondary until 02:00 UTC? any coverage gaps? :calendar:
Raj K: I can cover until 01:30 UTC then I have a calendar block. if it extends beyond 01:30 please page me and I can try to extend.
Maya P: gap from 01:30-02:00 then — Alex, are you available as backup after 01:30? otherwise I'll escalate to oncall-sre rotation.
Alex S: I can be on-call remotely after 01:30 for high-sev pages, but won't be able to hop into the bridge realistically. if it ramps up escalate to oncall-sre.
Maya P: action items for my shift:
- monitor eviction rate and p95 latency for embeddings (alert: embeddings.eviction_rate > 3/s sustained 5m)
- if eviction_rate > 6/s or p95 latency > 1.5s -> perform emergency cache flush for the problematic pod group per runbook
- keep prefetched off until steady-state for 30m
- continue customer throttling for the top-3 noisy customers and coordinate with CS to message affected accounts
- check memory pressure on nodes; if memory saturation > 80% consider cordoning the most pressure-heavy nodes and rolling them out
Raj K: I'll keep an eye on the routing layer logs for any retry storms. if we see the retry loop increase, add a temporary 50ms jitter to client retry middleware on the edge (we have a safe toggle: edge.retry_jitter = true)
Maya P: quick note re: tickets — CS opened TICK-8129 for customer A, TICK-8131 for customer B. escalation contact for customer A is mary@customer.com, CS has interim mitigation applied.
Alex S: diagnostic snippets if needed:
```
# top eviction pods
kubectl -n embeddings get pods | grep cache-worker | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl -n embeddings exec {} -- sh -c 'cat /proc/meminfo | head -n 5'
# check metrics quick
curl "http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=rate(embeddings_kv_evictions[2m])"
```
Maya P: if we need to roll back the prefetch flag it's: curl -X POST ... '{"value":true}'. But we should only re-enable once p95 < 1s for 15m.
SRE Bot: reminder: pager policy: P1 pages primary + escalation after 5m to rotation. P2 pages primary only. Adjust pages if you are stepping out of coverage.
Maya P: I'll update the bridge notes and add a short checklist at top. tagging @oncall-rotation in case we need a ramped escalation later.
Raj K: leaving a runbook pointer in-thread for the emergency cache flush step (copying from runbook):
```
# emergency cache flush for embeddings group
kubectl -n embeddings exec deploy/embeddings-cache-worker -- /bin/flush_cache --group hot_shards
sleep 10
# confirm eviction rate drops
```
Maya P: thanks. small ask — keep any large-scale config changes off the table unless we get explicit signoff from eng-platform or SRE lead.
Alex S: agreed. escalation path: pager -> oncall lead (sre-lead@redwood) -> eng-platform if we need infra changes.
Maya P: final handoff note: primary = Maya P (pager on), secondary = Raj K, backup = Alex S for P1 only. coverage gap 01:30-02:00 UTC; if incident escalates during that window page oncall-rotation immediately. bridge: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-77
Raj K: ack, monitoring and logs checked, will call out any regressions. ping me on Slack or page if anything spikes. :+1:
Alex S: thanks team — leaving the bridge now. I'll be reachable for P1 pages. good luck.
Maya P: taking over. I'll post a short status update in the morning handoff thread with any follow-ups. good luck and thanks. :coffee:
